description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

The State of Michigan’s Department of Technology, Management and Budget (DTMB) is hiring a junior application developer to support systems used by several state agencies. The role assists with application coding, testing, maintenance, enhancements, and implementation while learning development tools and working with senior staff, clients, vendors, and DTMB leadership.
Junior Application Developer supporting public-sector applications with coding, testing, maintenance, and guided system enhancements

Responsibilities:
• This position supports application development activities for systems used by the Department of Attorney General (AG), Michigan State Housing Development Authority (MSHDA), Michigan Occupational Safety & Health Administration (MIOSHA), and the Unemployment Insurance Appellate Commission (UIAC)
• The junior developer assists with coding, testing, and maintenance tasks that help meet each agency’s business needs
• Under the guidance of senior developers, this role contributes to system updates and enhancements and learns how new features and functions are designed to work within existing architectures
• This position supports other team members by assisting with technical tasks and learning to use development tools and agency systems
• The role participates in various phases of the software development lifecycle with guidance from senior staff and contractors
• Responsibilities include helping with the design, development, testing, and implementation of applications and system enhancements, as well as gaining exposure to new tools and technologies that support agency modernization efforts
• As part of a collaborative technical team, this position works with clients, vendors, and DTMB leadership to contribute to reliable solutions that meet key business needs while building skills and experience in the development platforms used by the organization

Requirements:
• Possession of a Bachelor's degree with 21 semester (32 term) credits in one or a combination of the following: computer science, data processing, computer information systems, data communications, networking, systems analysis, computer programming, information assurance, IT project management or mathematics
• No specific type or amount is required
• Possession of an associate's degree with 16 semester (24 term) credits in computer science, information assurance, data processing, computer information, data communications, networking, systems analysis, computer programming, IT project management, or mathematics and two years of experience as an application programmer, computer operator, or information technology technician; or two years (4,160 hours) of experience as an Information Technology Student Assistant may be substituted for the education requirement
• Educational level typically acquired through completion of high school and four years of experience as an application programmer, computer operator, information technology technician, or four years (8,320 hours) of experience as an Information Technology Student Assistant may be substituted for the education requirement
